theme: Presenting mixed results in a meeting
theme_zh: 在會議上報告好壞參半的數字
summary_zh: 學會用 although、despite、whereas、however 把「好消息＋壞消息」說清楚，季度報告、簡報時回答「我們的進度有跟上嗎？」都用得上。

vocab.definition: a small, usually temporary fall in an amount or level
vocab.example: There was a dip in sales in August.
vocab.example_zh: 八月的銷售額有小幅下滑。

vocab.example: We saw a spike in shipping costs in July.

vocab.definition: not going up or down; staying at the same level
vocab.example: Store sales stayed flat for the whole quarter.

vocab.definition: to do better than someone, something, or a forecast
vocab.example: The new product continues to outperform our forecast.
vocab.example_zh: 新產品的表現持續優於我們的預測。

vocab.definition: to balance one effect with an opposite effect
vocab.example: Lower packaging costs helped offset the higher shipping costs.
vocab.example_zh: 包裝成本降低，抵銷了部分運費的增加。

vocab.example: Marketing took the lion's share of the extra budget.
vocab.example_zh: 行銷拿走了追加預算的大部分。

vocab.definition: as a result of something that happened earlier
vocab.example: Sales rose on the back of the September promotion.
vocab.example_zh: 靠著九月的促銷，銷售額上升了。

vocab.definition: a list that shows how a total is divided into parts
vocab.example: Slide 6 shows a breakdown of sales by region.
vocab.example_zh: 第 6 頁是各區域銷售的細項。

reading.title: Before the Q3 Review
paragraphs: Hi team, just a heads-up before Thursday's Q3 review. I've been going through the numbers all week, and here's the short version so everyone can get up to speed before the meeting.

Overall revenue grew by 9% compared with the same quarter last year. Although that sounds healthy, almost all of the growth came from one channel. Online sales did most of the work: they outperformed our forecast by 14%, on the back of the September promotion. Store sales, however, stayed flat, and in August there was a clear dip when two stores closed for renovation.

Despite the strong online results, we're slightly behind our annual target, mainly because costs rose faster than expected. Shipping costs had a big spike in July, whereas packaging costs actually fell. The savings on packaging offset some of the increase, but not all of it. Marketing also took the lion's share of the extra budget, so expect questions about that.

I'll show a full breakdown by region on slide 6. If the director asks whether we're on track for the year, the honest answer is "nearly." Although we fell behind in Q3, a good holiday season should close the gap.

Finally, thanks to Leo for covering the dashboard while I was under the weather on Monday. I owe you one! Please send me any comments by Wednesday noon so I can get the slides signed off. Thanks, Anna

questions.q: Where did most of the revenue growth come from?
options: The new stores that opened in August
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：「Online sales did most of the work」，線上銷售比預測多 14%。

questions.q: Why is the team slightly behind its annual target?
options: Online sales were lower than forecast.
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：「mainly because costs rose faster than expected」，尤其是七月運費暴增。

questions.q: What can we infer about how the writer feels about the year as a whole?
options: She thinks the annual target is now impossible.
She is cautiously hopeful that the target can still be reached.
She believes the team is far ahead of plan.
She blames Leo for the Q3 results.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第四段她說，如果主管問今年進度跟不跟得上，誠實的答案是「nearly」（差不多），而且好的年終旺季「should close the gap」，表示審慎樂觀。

grammar.point: Linking contrast: although, despite, whereas, however

guide.key_zh: although 接句子、despite 接名詞或 V-ing；whereas 對比兩件事；however 開新句轉折。

uses.label_zh: 儘管（後面接名詞或 V-ing）

uses.note_zh: 放句首時前面用句號（或分號），後面加逗號；也可放句中，前後加逗號

mistakes.wrong: Although sales rose, but profits fell.
mistakes.why_zh: although 和 but 不能同時用

mistakes.wrong: Despite of the delay, we finished on time.
mistakes.right: Despite the delay, we finished on time.
mistakes.why_zh: despite 後面直接接名詞，不加 of（in spite of 才有 of）
despite 後面不能接完整句子；要接句子就用 although

examples.en: Although revenue grew, we're slightly behind our target.
examples.zh: 雖然營收成長了，我們還是略落後目標。

examples.en: Despite the dip in August, we're still close to plan.
examples.zh: 儘管八月有下滑，我們還是很接近計畫。

examples.en: Online sales beat our forecast by 14%, whereas store sales stayed flat.
examples.zh: 線上銷售比預測多 14%，而門市銷售持平。

examples.en: Shipping costs spiked in July. However, packaging costs fell.
examples.zh: 七月運費暴增。然而，包裝成本下降了。

exercises.q: ___ the launch was delayed, we still hit our Q3 target. (雖然)
exercises.explain_zh: 後面接完整句子（the launch was delayed），用 Although。

exercises.q: ___ the dip in August, the south still grew by 2% for the quarter. (儘管)
exercises.explain_zh: 後面接名詞片語 the dip in August，用 Despite（不加 of）。

exercises.q: The north beat its target, ___ the south missed it by 3%. (而)
exercises.explain_zh: 對比兩件不同的事，句中用 whereas（也可用 while）。

exercises.q: Our online ads cost less than last year. ___, they brought in fewer new customers. (然而)
exercises.explain_zh: 前面是句號、開新句子轉折，用 However，後面加逗號。

exercises.q: ___ having a smaller budget, the Taipei team outperformed every other region.
exercises.explain_zh: 後面接 V-ing（having），只能用 Despite；Although 和 Whereas 後面要接完整句子。
Although 已經表示轉折，後半句直接接句子，不再加 but 或 however。

review.point: Present perfect continuous for ongoing situations
review.point_zh: 現在完成進行式：從過去持續到現在的事

exercises.q: I ___ (work) on the Q3 slides since Monday, and they're almost done.
exercises.explain_zh: 從星期一持續到現在、還在做，用 have been + V-ing。

exercises.q: Leo ___ (help) Anna with the regional numbers all week, so the slides are almost ready.
exercises.explain_zh: 主詞 Leo 是第三人稱單數，從這週開始一直幫忙到現在，用 has been + V-ing。

exercises.q: Online sales ___ steadily for three months, so we're hopeful about Q4.
exercises.explain_zh: 持續三個月到現在用 have been + V-ing。rise 是不及物動詞，沒有被動，所以 have been risen 錯；are rising 是現在進行式，不能搭配 for three months 表示「持續到現在」；單純現在式 rise 也不行。

guide.key_zh: 從過去開始、到現在還在持續的事，用 have/has been + V-ing

uses.label_zh: 從過去一直持續到現在（還在進行）
uses.signal: for two weeks, since August, lately, all day

uses.label_zh: 看到現在的樣子，推測剛剛一直在做什麼

mistakes.wrong: I've been seeing three apartments this week.
mistakes.right: I've seen three apartments this week.
mistakes.why_zh: 講次數、結果用現在完成式，不用進行式

mistakes.wrong: I've been knowing him for years.
mistakes.why_zh: know、like、own 這類狀態動詞通常不用進行式

mistakes.wrong: I've been working here since three years.
mistakes.right: I've been working here for three years.
mistakes.why_zh: for 接一段時間，since 接開始的時間點

timeline.label: I've been looking for an apartment since August.
I saw one yesterday.
timeline.note_zh: 對照：過去式，一個時間點

listening.title: Fixing slide 6

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Anna
lines.text: Leo, thanks for staying late. Do you have a minute to go through slide 6 with me?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Sure. By the way, are you feeling better? You were running a fever on Monday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Anna
lines.text: Much better, thanks. So, the regional breakdown. Although the north did well, I'm worried the chart makes the south look worse than it is.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Yeah, the south had that dip in August, but that was the store renovations, not demand.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Anna
lines.text: Exactly. Despite the closures, their online sales actually went up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Then why don't we add a note on the slide? Something like "two stores closed for six weeks".

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Anna
lines.text: Good idea. I'll add the note. Could you double-check the shipping figures? I think the July spike is slightly off.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: No problem. I'll have them to you by ten tomorrow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Anna
lines.text: Perfect. That's the last thing I need before the director signs off on the deck.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Last quarter we were still fixing slides at midnight the night before, whereas this time we're actually ahead of schedule.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Anna
lines.text: Don't jinx it! But yes, I think we're in good shape.

questions.q: Who will add the note about the store closures to slide 6?
questions.explain_zh: Leo 提議加註記後，Anna 說「Good idea. I'll add the note.」；Leo 負責的是重新核對運費數字。

questions.q: Why did the south's numbers drop in August?
options: Two stores were closed for renovation.
questions.explain_zh: Leo 說八月的下滑是「the store renovations, not demand」，接著建議在投影片上註明「two stores closed for six weeks」。

questions.q: What can we infer about last quarter's presentation?
options: It was prepared in a rush at the last minute.
It was finished well ahead of time.
Leo was not involved in it.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：Leo 說上一季「we were still fixing slides at midnight the night before」，這次才「ahead of schedule」，可見上次是最後一刻才趕完。

dictation: I'll have them to you by ten tomorrow.
That's the last thing I need before the director signs off on the deck.
Despite the closures, their online sales actually went up.

shadowing: Although revenue grew, we're slightly behind our target.
Online sales rose, whereas store sales stayed flat.
Despite the dip in August, we're still close to plan.
However, costs rose faster than we expected.

prompts.question: In one sentence, report a number from your work using although or despite.
prompts.question_zh: 用一句話報告一個你工作上的數字，句子裡要用 although 或 despite。
prompts.sample: Although we got fewer orders this month, the average order value went up.

prompts.question: Your manager asks, "Are we on track?" Give a one-sentence honest answer.
prompts.question_zh: 主管問：「我們的進度有跟上嗎？」用一句話老實回答。
prompts.sample: Mostly, although we fell behind in August because two stores were closed.

writing.task: Write a short email to your manager summarizing a quarter's results before a meeting. Include (1) one piece of good news, (2) one problem, and (3) one suggestion for next quarter.
writing.task_zh: 會議前寫一封簡短的 email 給主管，總結這一季的成果。內容包括：(1) 一個好消息；(2) 一個問題；(3) 一個下一季的建議。
writing.sample: Hi Karen, here's a quick summary of our Q3 results before Thursday's meeting. Overall, revenue grew by 9%. Although that is good news, most of the growth came from online sales, whereas store sales stayed flat. Despite the strong online numbers, we are slightly behind our annual target because shipping costs rose sharply in July. However, I think we can close the gap in Q4 if the holiday promotion does as well as September's did. I'd suggest that we review the shipping contract next month. Let me know if you need the full breakdown before the meeting. Best, Mimi
checklist_zh: 有沒有包含好消息、問題、建議三部分
although 後面接完整句子，despite 後面接名詞或 V-ing
However 放在句首，後面加逗號

translation.zh: 雖然新產品晚了一個月上市，它還是超越了我們的預測。（用 although）
translation.en: Although the new product launched a month late, it still outperformed our forecast.
alt: Although the new product was launched a month late, it still outperformed our forecast.
Although the new product launched a month late, it still beat our forecast.

translation.zh: 儘管預算比較少，台北團隊的進度還是跟得上。（用 despite）
translation.en: Despite a smaller budget, the Taipei team is still on track.
alt: Despite having a smaller budget, the Taipei team is still on track.
Despite its smaller budget, the Taipei team is still on track.

translation.zh: 行銷拿走了大部分的預算，而業務只拿到 10%。（用 whereas）
translation.en: Marketing took the lion's share of the budget, whereas the sales team got only 10%.
alt: Marketing took the lion's share of the budget, whereas the sales team only got 10%.
Marketing got most of the budget, whereas the sales team got only 10%.

translation.zh: 營收成長了 9%。然而，成本成長得更快。（用 however）
translation.en: Revenue grew by 9%. However, costs grew even faster.
alt: Revenue grew by 9%. However, costs rose even faster.
Revenue went up by 9%. However, costs went up even faster.

translation.zh: 我從星期一就一直在準備這份簡報。（已經…一直在…）
translation.en: I've been preparing this presentation since Monday.
alt: I have been preparing this presentation since Monday.
I've been working on this presentation since Monday.

reading.title: When the Numbers Tell Two Stories
paragraphs: Every analyst eventually faces the same dilemma: the headline number looks great, while the figures underneath are quietly flashing red. Last quarter, Ken found himself in exactly that position. On paper, it was a triumph: subscriptions had jumped by a fifth. Yet nearly half of the new customers had signed up through a heavily discounted trial, and early data suggested many of them would cancel the moment full pricing kicked in.

His first draft of the deck led with the growth chart and tucked the cancellation figures into an appendix. Although nothing in it was technically misleading, his manager, Rachel, sent it straight back. "If the board finds this on page twenty, they'll wonder what else we've buried," she wrote. "Lead with the tension, not the trophy."

So Ken rebuilt the story. The opening slide now put the two numbers side by side: twenty percent more subscribers, but a projected retention rate well below target. He also cut three slides of upbeat charts that, frankly, only distracted from the main point. Rather than glossing over the problem, he spelled out what the team didn't yet know and what it would take to find out: a six-week test comparing two pricing tiers. Despite his fear that the board would pounce on the bad news, the meeting turned out to be the smoothest he had sat through all year. One director even thanked him for not dressing the numbers up.

The lesson stuck with him. Presenting mixed results isn't about softening the blow or hiding it; it's about earning enough trust that people believe your good news too. However tempting it is to lead with the win, a presenter who flags the risks first rarely gets caught off guard by the follow-up questions.

questions.q: Why did Rachel send Ken's first draft back?
options: The growth chart contained a calculation error.
Hiding the cancellation data could make the board distrust the whole deck.
The deck was too long for a board meeting.
She wanted him to remove the cancellation figures completely.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：她說「they'll wonder what else we've buried」，把壞消息藏在附錄會讓董事會懷疑還藏了什麼。

questions.q: What did Ken propose to find out what the team didn't yet know?
options: A survey of customers who had cancelled
A six-week test comparing two pricing tiers
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：「a six-week test comparing two pricing tiers」。

questions.q: What does Rachel mean by "Lead with the tension, not the trophy"?
options: Open with the problem next to the success, not just the success.
Avoid mentioning the growth at all.
Start the presentation with a joke to reduce stress.
Let the board ask about the problem first.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：tension 指好壞數字的矛盾，trophy 指亮眼成績；第三段 Ken 改成開場就把兩個數字並排。

questions.q: Why did the meeting probably go so smoothly?
options: The board did not notice the retention problem.
The subscription numbers improved before the meeting.
Ken's openness made the board trust him and his plan.
Rachel presented the bad news for him.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：有董事感謝他「for not dressing the numbers up」，最後一段也說誠實報告能「earning enough trust」。

listening.title: Rehearsing the opening

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Okay, run me through the opening. Pretend I'm the board.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ken
lines.text: Right. So, um, this quarter subscriptions grew by twenty percent, which is—

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Stop there. You've already lost me. What's the catch?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ken
lines.text: The catch is... well, almost half of those people came in on the discounted trial.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: And?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ken
lines.text: And if they cancel at the rate we're seeing, retention drops to about sixty percent, while our target's seventy-five.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Good. Say that first. Don't make them dig for it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ken
lines.text: Won't it sound like I'm panicking, though?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Not if you follow it right away with the plan. What's the plan?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ken
lines.text: A six-week test of two pricing tiers. We'll know by mid-January whether the cheaper tier keeps people.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: There you go. Bad news, then a plan, then a date. That's what they'll remember.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ken
lines.text: Got it. Although, honestly, I'd still rather open with the twenty percent.

options: Open with the growth figure and skip the problem.
State the problem first and follow it with a plan and a date.
Wait for the board to ask about cancellations.
Cancel the discounted trial before the meeting.
questions.explain_zh: Rachel 說「Say that first」，最後總結「Bad news, then a plan, then a date」。

questions.q: Why is Ken uneasy about opening with the problem?
options: He doesn't have a plan yet.
He thinks it might make him look like he's panicking.
The board has already seen the figures.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：他問「Won't it sound like I'm panicking, though?」，最後一句也說還是比較想從 20% 開場。
Ken 說留存率可能掉到 60%，「while our target's seventy-five」。

dictation: Don't make them dig for it.
We'll know by mid-January whether the cheaper tier keeps people.
Bad news, then a plan, then a date.

glossary.definition: treating a problem as if it were not important
to quickly criticize or attack a mistake or weakness

glossary.zh: 把數字包裝得比較好看
glossary.definition: presenting figures so they look better than they really are
making bad news easier to accept

glossary.zh: 不管多麼誘人（這裡的 however = no matter how，不是「然而」）
glossary.definition: no matter how tempting it is
